One ALZ decoder support, 2026-10-10

Base: bzip2 1.0.8, Julian Seward, copyright 1996-2019.
Source: https://deb.debian.org/debian/pool/main/b/bzip2/bzip2_1.0.8.orig.tar.gz
SHA256: ab5a03176ee106d3f0fa90e381da478ddae405918153cca248e682cd0c4a2269
The original LICENSE is retained. This is an altered version.

The minimal framing changes follow Kippler's zlib-licensed UnAlz 0.65:
https://deb.debian.org/debian/pool/main/u/unalz/unalz_0.65.orig.tar.gz
SHA256: 4c26699eb7545072de2ef7de79b4fff1f01c4db09cebff2d8d50ec03d5d74db0
Its original permission notice is retained in UNALZ-LICENSE.txt.
No old UnAlz parser, path writer, bundled zlib, or bundled bzip2 is shipped.

one-alz.patch records every change to the upstream C source and headers:
- Per-stream ALZ mode and BZ2_alzDecompressInit; standard BZh mode remains.
- Separate initial coroutine state; ALZ implies a 900k block limit.
- DLZ01/DLZ02 framing replaces the standard block/end markers.
- ALZ omits block CRCs, combined CRC, and the randomisation bit.
- Standard mode retains its original CRC and bitstream validation.

The caller MUST verify the ALZ container CRC32 and exact expanded size.
One does so for every decoded file, including encrypted files, with bounded
input/output buffers, global output/time limits and checked file writes.
BZ_NO_STDIO disables the library's filesystem/stdout wrappers. Invariant
failures terminate the disposable archive helper with a protocol error.

Do not use the ALZ mode to decode ordinary .bz2 streams. One's existing
BZIP2 archive support continues to use the packaged 7-Zip handler.
